PyTorch explicitly warns that batched matrix multiplication and individually sliced multiplication can produce different floating-point results, even with identical inputs. Changing catalog chunk size or user batch size can therefore perturb frozen HSTU scores and reverse near-tied rankings. TF32 reduces input mantissa precision; FP16/BF16 reductions add further numerical differences. Seeds alone cannot establish shape-independent scores. [PyTorch numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)

Practical implication: compare identical user–item pairs across the actual candidate-scoring and catalog-chunking paths, including partial final chunks. Measure maximum absolute/relative score differences, nonfinite values, target-rank changes, and top-10 membership changes; numerical closeness alone does not guarantee ranking agreement. Use evaluation mode, disable autocast for an FP32 diagnostic reference, explicitly select full FP32 matmul precision, and keep hardware/software settings fixed. FP64 rescoring can diagnose close comparisons but does not establish equivalence to the pinned evaluator’s arithmetic. [Matmul precision controls](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.set_float32_matmul_precision.html)

For defensible target ranks, obtain the target score from the same computed candidate-score vector used for comparisons, rather than a separate singleton multiplication. Match the host evaluator’s exact tie convention: counting strictly greater scores differs from counting greater-or-equal scores. PyTorch documents that `topk` does not guarantee stable indices for ties, even with sorted output. Record exact ties and near-tie margins; do not introduce epsilon ties or change evaluator ordering. These are methodological implications of the documented numerical behavior. [PyTorch topk](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.topk.html)
